fivetran.name: Fivetran
fivetran.summary: A managed service that runs the connectors for you and bills on monthly active rows.
fivetran.bestWhen: you want a vendor to own connector upkeep and you would rather pay a meter than hire an engineer.
fivetran.watchOut: every connection has its own cost curve, and the paid rates sit in a separate Service Consumption Table.

hevo.name: Hevo
hevo.summary: A hosted tool billed on events, with a 14-day free trial.
hevo.bestWhen: you are a small team with common SaaS sources and want to try it free for 14 days first.
hevo.watchOut: a row updated five times counts as five events, and it offers a trial rather than a free plan.

integrate.name: Integrate.io
integrate.summary: A managed ETL tool with a flat fee and a 60-second pipeline frequency.
integrate.bestWhen: you move large, steady volumes and want a bill that does not change with row counts.
integrate.watchOut: $1,999 a month is a lot at low volume, and 60 seconds is near-real-time, not streaming.

estuary.name: Estuary
estuary.summary: A managed streaming tool with real-time delivery, log-based change capture and a free tier.
estuary.bestWhen: you need real-time delivery and want to start without a sales call.
estuary.watchOut: each source and destination is a billed instance, and for Iceberg its main connector needs S3 and EMR Serverless Spark.

airbyte.name: Airbyte
airbyte.summary: A large connector library you can self-host under the Elastic License 2.0, with a free Core and a cloud option.
airbyte.bestWhen: you have engineers, want a large connector catalog you can self-host, and like having a cloud option later.
airbyte.watchOut: Core uses the Elastic License 2.0, CDC runs as scheduled syncs, and Cloud Standard prices doubled in September 2026.

dlt.name: dlt
dlt.summary: A free Python library where a pipeline is a small piece of code.
dlt.bestWhen: your team writes Python and likes pipelines kept as code.
dlt.watchOut: there is no point-and-click setup, and its only built-in change data capture source is Postgres replication.

glue.name: AWS Glue
glue.summary: An AWS service that runs Spark jobs and reads and writes Iceberg tables.
glue.bestWhen: your data and team are already inside AWS and someone can write Spark jobs.
glue.watchOut: there is no free ETL tier, and it is not simple point-and-click replication.

adf.name: Azure Data Factory
adf.summary: An Azure service with a visual designer and plenty of connectors.
adf.bestWhen: you are on Azure and want a visual designer.
adf.watchOut: Microsoft's docs point new users to Fabric Data Factory, and its Iceberg sink writes only to Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2.

olake.name: OLake Go
olake.summary: An open-source tool that copies databases into Apache Iceberg or Parquet on storage you control, free to self-host.
olake.bestWhen: you want database changes in Iceberg on storage you run, with change capture for Postgres, MySQL and MariaDB, MongoDB and SQL Server.
olake.watchOut: its output is Iceberg and Parquet, so it suits teams that want one of those on storage they run.
